column1: How is the imperfecto de subjuntivo formed?
column2:
Take the ellos form of the preterite, drop -ron, add:

-ra set: ra · ras · ra · ramos · rais · ran
-se set: se · ses · se · semos · seis · sen

hablaron → habla- · comieron → comie- · fueron → fue-

No exceptions at all. The nosotros form takes an accent: habláramos.

column1:
When and why do you use the
Imperfecto de subjuntivo?
column2:
Two distinct jobs.
  • Backshifting — everything that took the present subjunctive takes this one once the main verb goes past. Quiero que vengas → quería que vinieras.
  • Counterfactual si clauses — si tuviera dinero, viajaría. The si clause takes this tense, the result clause the conditional. (Real open conditions use si + present indicative: si tengo tiempo, voy.)
  • Ojalá + this tense = unlikely or impossible wish. Ojalá viniera vs ojalá venga.
  • Softened requests, -ra forms only — quisiera un café; ¿pudiera usted…?
  • Como si, always — habla como si fuera experto.

column1:
Tricks and tips for the
Imperfecto de subjuntivo
column2:
• The most regular tense in Spanish — zero exceptions. Know the preterite and you know this free.
  • -ra and -se are interchangeable in every subjunctive use. -ra dominates in speech and in Latin America; -se is more literary and more common in Spain. Two -ra-only jobs: polite requests (quisiera, never quisiese) and the journalistic pluperfect (el edificio que construyera en 1920 = había construido).
  • The nosotros form takes an accent and shifts stress: habláramos, comiéramos.
  • yo and él are identical.
  • Drill si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional as a sentence shape, not two separate rules.
